name: Echinodorus
taxonomic_scope: Echinodorus sensu Flora of North America for source-pool names. Kew POWO currently places E. cordifolius under Aquarius cordifolius; preserve source-pool labels and hand off accepted-concept mapping rather than creating a new species card.
look_here_first: Follow the complete flowering/fruiting axis. An erect, non-proliferating axis points toward E. berteroi; an arching or ground-hugging axis that often roots or produces plantlets at nodes points toward E. cordifolius. Confirm by examining the tiny veins on a sepal back and glands/ribs on a mature achene.
shared_traits: Rooted shallow-water or mudflat Alismataceae herbs with basal long-petioled leaves and translucent linear leaf markings.
Flowers in spaced whorls, each with three sepals, three petals, numerous stamens and many separate carpels; mature achenes aggregate into rounded burrlike heads.
Emergent leaf blades may be ovate to cordate in either species; leaf outline alone is not a dependable species key.

comparison_matrix.character: Mature inflorescence axis and vegetative plantlets
comparison_matrix.berteroi: Erect raceme (rarely panicle), generally non-proliferating; 1–9 whorls.
comparison_matrix.cordifolius: Arching to decumbent or prostrate raceme, frequently proliferating/rooting at nodes; 3–9 whorls.
comparison_matrix.diagnostic_weight: HIGH on mature plants; follow the full axis, not a cropped tip.
HIGH with macro lens; compare multiple mature sepals.

comparison_matrix.character: Stamen count in a fresh open flower
comparison_matrix.diagnostic_weight: HIGH when countable; photograph with petals displaced and a scale.
Supporting reproductive distinction; intact flower needed.

comparison_matrix.cordifolius: Usually 2.1–7.5 cm, erect to ascending; substantial overlap at 2.1–2.8 cm.

comparison_matrix.berteroi: Typically 1–2 facial glands, often 2 keels; about 3–5 ribs.
comparison_matrix.cordifolius: Typically 3–4 facial glands, often 1 keel; about 3–4 ribs.
comparison_matrix.diagnostic_weight: HIGH with ripe separated achenes at magnification; count several.

comparison_matrix.berteroi: About 2.6–15.5 cm long; elliptic, lanceolate or ovate.
comparison_matrix.cordifolius: About 6.5–32 cm long; usually ovate to elliptic.
comparison_matrix.diagnostic_weight: LOW: size overlaps and depends strongly on water depth and vigor.

decision_sequence: Confirm Echinodorus-like burrhead: rooted aquatic basal rosette, whorled three-part flowers, many small achenes in each rounded fruit head.
Photograph the entire reproductive axis at maturity: erect/non-proliferating favors berteroi; arching/prostrate with rooted nodes or plantlets favors cordifolius.
Magnify sepal undersides: smooth veins favor berteroi; papillate roughened veins favor cordifolius.
Count stamens in fresh flowers and achene facial glands in ripe fruit; use at least two independent reproductive characters.
If plants are sterile, young, or show mixed states, retain Echinodorus/Aquarius sp. and request targeted diagnostic review rather than forcing an ID.
overlap_cautions: Both species may have heart-shaped leaves, translucent leaf lines, whorled flowers, and rounded fruit heads. Leaf base and flower color do not separate them.
A young cordifolius axis can initially stand upright; use mature flowering/fruiting stalks before relying on posture.
Pedicel length overlaps, and gland/rib characters require fully mature achenes.

Some floras recognize cordifolius in Aquarius. Treat Echinodorus cordifolius as a source-pool/FNA comparison label until the accepted-name mapping is reviewed; do not infer a separate canonical concept.
The Master Plant Pool includes both names, but neither has a canonical species.json in the checked manifest. Genus lesson is provisional and does not certify native-range status.

lookalikes.separator: Sagittaria typically has unisexual flowers with female flowers below male on the axis; Echinodorus flowers are bisexual with numerous stamens and carpels together. Both can have non-arrow-shaped leaves.
Compare achene head structure and flower architecture; Echinodorus forms compact rounded burrlike heads at spaced axis nodes. Verify with mature achenes, not leaf shape.
Do not infer wild provenance or native-range status from a pond planting. Check flower, sepal and achene characters and collection context.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.shot: Include entire stalk from rosette to terminal whorl, plus node inset and centimeter scale.
10–20× macro of several sepals from each species, with arrows to veins and mm scale.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.character: 9–15 vs ~20–22 stamens and clawed vs unclawed petals
diagnostic_photo_checklist.shot: Overhead macro of open flower with petals parted; label counted stamens and petal base.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.character: Facial glands (1–2 vs 3–4), ribs and keels
diagnostic_photo_checklist.shot: Matched side and back views at 20× with mm scale and labeled glands.
Two or more fruiting nodes, measured pedicels and node-to-node view.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.character: Overlapping leaf shape and submerged/emergent variation
diagnostic_photo_checklist.shot: Leaf base and backlit pellucid lines from documented plants; teach why leaves alone mislead.
Existing Sagittaria platyphylla project/Joey frame when identification and reuse permit; annotate sex positions.

handoffs: Taxonomy + Diagnostic Review: resolve Echinodorus cordifolius (FNA/World Flora Online) versus Aquarius cordifolius (Kew POWO) accepted-name mapping; retain source-pool name as alias if warranted. Do not install duplicate concepts.
Approved Taxa Installer: source-pool E. berteroi and E. cordifolius lack canonical species cards; install only after accepted-concept mapping and normal species pipeline.
Diagnostic Photo Polish: source matched diagnostic photos of sepal vein papillae, stamen counts, mature achene glands, and full reproductive axes. Do not use unsourced placeholder images.
Family Backfill: link this aquatic Echinodorus comparison against existing Sagittaria platyphylla family anchor when convenient; preserve existing family lesson.
